interest: This document is valuable to diplomatic and intelligence historians as an official archival record illustrating how the U.S. State Department monitored clandestine Japanese espionage and propaganda networks targeted at the Soviet Far East during the 1930s. It points to significant episodes of interwar intrigue, including the dubious activities of international operative D. F. Giera and Soviet public trials of alleged Japanese spies in the Far Eastern Krai. Additionally, it serves as an indispensable finding aid and administrative trail, providing researchers with exact file citations and cross-references (such as 811.113/381) to trace related State Department intelligence records across posts in Moscow, Harbin, and Peiping.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State "List of Papers" (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, cataloging documents filed under decimal file 894.20261 concerning Japanese military activities and intelligence gathering in the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. The docket sheet lists three separate items produced between 1934 and 1939: a January 1934 memorandum by Joseph C. Green of the Western European Division concerning claims by D. F. Giera that he was a Japanese secret agent employing operatives in the USSR; a March 1936 despatch from Ambassador William C. Bullitt in Moscow reporting on trials of Japanese spies and Soviet press commentary in the Far Eastern Krai; and a June 1939 despatch from Consul George R. Merrell in Harbin transmitting a report to the Embassy in Peiping regarding Japanese intelligence-gathering and propaganda endeavors. Although the primary records were cross-referenced or filed elsewhere, this inventory serves as an official institutional record of U.S. diplomatic monitoring of Japanese espionage operations in Soviet East Asia.

subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State Form DS-46 ('List of Papers') dated October 12, 1945, listing documents under decimal file 894.20261 regarding Japanese military intelligence and activities in the USSR. It indexes three items spanning 1934 to 1939: a memorandum by Joseph C. Green concerning D. F. Giera's claims of being a Japanese secret agent with operatives in the USSR, a despatch from Ambassador William C. Bullitt regarding Soviet spy trials in the Far Eastern Krai, and a despatch from George R. Merrell in Harbin reporting on Japanese intelligence collection and propaganda. The sheet details document numbers, origins, dates, State Department distribution routings, and subject purports.
